conventions.convention: Use natural units c=ℏ=1, dimensionless actions, normalized positive Borel probability measures, and explicitly integrable complex Boltzmann weights. Complex logarithms are chosen continuously on nonzero patches with compatible transition phases.
The Wilsonian step subtracts c_j from minus the logarithm of the high-field integral. Consequently Z_next=e^{c_j}Z_previous and W_UV−W_IR=C, where C is single-valued and admissibly local.

The local anomaly quotient uses the same background-only finite-jet complex and the same linear counterterm and boundary-primitive spaces at both endpoints. Identifying variations of W with local anomaly densities requires the explicitly assumed linear, Wick-rotation-compatible representative assignment.

The determinant line is (det ker D⁺)* tensor det coker D⁺. Loop holonomy closes path transport with the inverse endpoint gauge map. Global matching additionally assumes a unitary connection-preserving line isomorphism that respects endpoint gauge identifications.

The mixed counterterm example admits only trivial U(1) bundles and transformations represented by smooth periodic real gauge parameters. Its coefficient k is real, with no large-gauge quantization assertion.
The lattice source j is fixed, real, nonzero, and does not transform as a spurion; m₀>0, λ>0, a>0, and N≥2.

The categorical problem uses strict underlying linear 2-categories with weak monoidal structure, retaining tensor comparisons, associators, unitors, and the pentagonator. Endpoint data are Hom categories Hom(x acting on b_D,b_D), with a specified nonzero vacuum surface; endability requires a nonzero endpoint object.

Under the stated finite-regulator exact symmetry-preserving comparison, common four-dimensional BRST/Wick-rotation and local-density compatibility hypotheses, and unitary connection-preserving determinant-line comparison respecting endpoint gauge identifications, the ultraviolet and complete infrared local BRST anomaly classes agree modulo the declared counterterms, and determinant-line holonomies agree on every admitted background loop modulo gauge transformations.

concerns.concern: The final compatibility paragraph fixes categorical backgrounds on an oriented 3-manifold but asks their invertible restriction to reproduce H^{1,4}_{C,N}(s|d_H) and the earlier chiral determinant-line holonomy. The cited local-anomaly definition expressly requires four-dimensional spacetime, and the cited chiral determinant-line definition requires even spacetime dimension. Thus 'where the earlier suppliers’ hypotheses apply' supplies no direct specialization to the fixed 2+1-dimensional theory. An explicit dimension-changing comparison or dimension-appropriate analogue is needed to make this compatibility subproblem nonvacuous. This concerns the formulation of the additional research question, not the proved matching theorem.

seams_checked.note: The theorem preserves the supplier's background-only four-dimensional quotient and restricted counterterm/boundary spaces. Its extra local-density compatibility assumption supplies the inference from the RG identity. The open problem restates that supplier faithfully, although its proposed cross-dimensional compatibility needs clarification as recorded in concerns.

The theorem retains the inverse determinant-line convention, admissible analytic data, and inverse endpoint gauge closure. Its connection-preserving comparison justifies conjugacy of loop endomorphisms. The open problem treats inflow and holonomy as restricted earlier interfaces, without asserting that they classify categorical anomalies.

This is a contextual page prerequisite; no assigned item invokes the Ising realization or coherence result as a logical premise. The opened Ising definition supplies ordinary fusion data, without braiding or physical realization, and the assigned page makes no stronger attribution.

The exact-RG definition uses finite high/low integrations and explicitly labels complex weights, extra sectors, nonvanishing, continuous logarithms, and background locality as additional supplied data. It does not attribute these extensions or continuum existence to the real-action Wilsonian supplier.

The open problem retains the supplier's underlying finite semisimple 2-category conventions and explicitly replaces its Gray-monoid tensor convention with weak monoidal data. Retaining a nontrivial pentagonator agrees with [Kong–Tian–Zhou, §2 and Remark 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.04644). The formulation distinguishes its adopted marked-interface question from the proposals in [Categorical Anomaly Matching, Appendix A.6](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.00982v1#A1.SS6).

The counterterm example uses the declared restricted local quotient and explicitly assumes the endpoint density identification. Its finite small-gauge variation has the displayed signs; the quadratic gauge-parameter term integrates to zero as an exact form. The breaking example correctly separates classical noninvariance from any quantum anomaly claim.
